Class Fighter

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.Fighter
public final class Fighter extends Object
The trained policy as a player, with no learning attached: everything between what it senses on one tick and what it presses. Whoever owns the body supplies the picture and the body's state and carries out the returned action; that is all that differs between playing the user's own character and playing a fake player.

Not thread-safe: one thread drives one fighter.

      public void crosshairOnOpponent(boolean on)
      To be told before every decision: whether the game has the opponent under the crosshair and within reach right now. What the rule about answering a hit goes by; see AnswerRule.

    • backOutRule

      public void backOutRule(boolean on)
      Whether backing out of a combo is a rule for it, as it is in training from the stage on that keeps the push for S; see Config.backRule.

    • answerForced

      public boolean answerForced()
      Whether the swing of the last decision was made by that rule. Such a swing is only to be carried out if the opponent is still under the crosshair.

    • answerCancelled

      public void answerCancelled()
      The rule's swing was not carried out: by the time of the click the opponent was no longer under the crosshair.

      public void swingNoEarlierThan(float charge)

    • decide

      public int[] decide(MaskFrame frame, BodyState body)
      One decision.
      Parameters:
      frame - the newest picture, with the camera angles it was taken at
      body - the body's state now; the hit clocks are filled in here
      Returns:
      the action, valid until the next call; turn the camera by yawRate() and pitchRate() rather than by the yaw and pitch heads

    • rules

      public int rules()
      Which rules had keys on the last decision, a bit each: answer swing, swing kept for the way down, run at a jumper, jump reset, backing out, step back, a jump made for it, camera after a hit, looking for a lost opponent, straight in. For the record of a fight.
